safety.judgement: The model's silence (no target organ; no cardiovascular signal in dog telemetry) was not contradicted in patients, and the reviewer states the comparison. Ombitasvir's review (Viekira Pak, Dec 2014) makes the same no-target-organ statement; one entry suffices. Rule question 4 settled: toxicology is scored per drug (track = model x drug x route), so daclatasvir's adrenal contra no longer overrides this ledipasvir result.

safety.magnitude_basis: adrenal cortical hypertrophy/hyperplasia predicted in rat and monkey; cortisol unchanged in patients
safety.population: Daclatasvir-treated patients in global and Japanese Phase 1 and Phase 3 trials (24-h urine cortisol)
safety.confidence_note: Read in the EMA EPAR text (EMA/419836/2014, CHMP opinion 26 June 2014, nonclinical section on the adrenal gland). The FDA summary review (2015) states the same: cortisol monitored in early trials, no effects noted.
safety.judgement: Rule question 3 settled: the adrenal cortical hypertrophy in rats and monkeys at about clinical exposure is a predicted harm, and patients measured for it (24-h urine cortisol) showed none, so contra, magnitude opposite. Rule question 5 settled: the EMA EPAR (June 2014) made the comparison before the FDA review, so the year is 2014. Toxicology is now scored per drug, so this contra sits on daclatasvir's track only. Daclatasvir's monkey liver findings are not scored: the clinical ALT signal was attributed to asunaprevir.
